chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadala from Aban from Mis'ma from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said:

My father (peace be upon him) considered for these two Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina) what he did not consider for others, and he said that completing the prayer in them is among the reserved (special) matters.

key_terms.الإِتمَامَ: Completion (of prayer, i.e., praying 4 rak'ahs instead of 2)
key_terms.المَذخُورِ: Reserved / Set aside (implying a special, distinct ruling)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on completing prayer in Mecca and Medina according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguished the two Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina) by prescribing full prayer (tamam) rather than the shortened prayer (qasr) typically observed elsewhere, a ruling rooted in their unique spiritual gravity. This specific legal status is described as 'al-amr al-madhur' (the reserved or stored matter), indicating a distinct, perhaps esoteric or highly specific, divine decree applicable exclusively to these holy sites. This view highlights the Shi'a emphasis on the intrinsic sanctity of the Prophet's and Imams' domains influencing ritual practice.
